question.:question/problem:
The path $C$ follows $y=x^{2}$ from $A(2,4)$ to $B(1,1)$. Evaluate

$$
\int_C \left(- x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Choose a coordinate parameter that keeps the curve smooth.

$$
x(t)=t,\qquad y(t)=t^{2}.
$$

The stated endpoints give $t=2$ at $A$ and $t=1$ at $B$; retain that order in the integral. Differentiation gives

$$
x'(t)=1,\qquad y'(t)=2 t.
$$

Write the coefficients of $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}y$ as $P$ and $Q$. Substitute both coordinates and multiply by the corresponding derivative. Denote the two contributions by $A(t)$ and $B(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(t)&=\left(- \left(t\right)\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=- t
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(t)&=\left(\left(t^{2}\right)\right)\cdot \left(2 t\right) \\ &=2 t^{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

The differential form uses the sum of these contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\int_{2}^{1}\left(A(t)+B(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{2}^{1}\left(2 t^{3} - t\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\left[\frac{t^{4}}{2} - \frac{t^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{1} \\ &=\left(0\right)-\left(6\right) \\ &=-6
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
The path $C$ follows $y=2 \pi x^{2}$ from $A(1,2 \pi)$ to $B(2,8 \pi)$. Evaluate

$$
\int_C \left(\cos{\left(\frac{y}{x^{2}} \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 4 x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Choose a coordinate parameter that keeps the curve smooth.

$$
x(t)=t,\qquad y(t)=2 \pi t^{2}.
$$

The stated endpoints give $t=1$ at $A$ and $t=2$ at $B$; retain that order in the integral. Differentiation gives

$$
x'(t)=1,\qquad y'(t)=4 \pi t.
$$

Write the coefficients of $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}y$ as $P$ and $Q$. Substitute both coordinates and multiply by the corresponding derivative. Denote the two contributions by $A(t)$ and $B(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(t)&=\left(\cos{\left(\frac{\left(2 \pi t^{2}\right)}{\left(t\right)^{2}} \right)}\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=\cos\left(2 \pi\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=1
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(t)&=\left(- 4 \left(t\right)^{2}\right)\cdot \left(4 \pi t\right) \\ &=- 16 \pi t^{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

The differential form uses the sum of these contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\int_{1}^{2}\left(A(t)+B(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{2}\left(- 16 \pi t^{3} + 1\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\left[- 4 \pi t^{4} + t\right]_{1}^{2} \\ &=\left(2 - 64 \pi\right)-\left(1 - 4 \pi\right) \\ &=1 - 60 \pi
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
The path $C$ follows $y=3 \pi x^{2}$ from $A(1,3 \pi)$ to $B(2,12 \pi)$. Evaluate

$$
\int_C \left(\sin{\left(\frac{y}{2 x^{2}} \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(- 3 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Choose a coordinate parameter that keeps the curve smooth.

$$
x(t)=t,\qquad y(t)=3 \pi t^{2}.
$$

The stated endpoints give $t=1$ at $A$ and $t=2$ at $B$; retain that order in the integral. Differentiation gives

$$
x'(t)=1,\qquad y'(t)=6 \pi t.
$$

Write the coefficients of $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}y$ as $P$ and $Q$. Substitute both coordinates and multiply by the corresponding derivative. Denote the two contributions by $A(t)$ and $B(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(t)&=\left(\sin{\left(\frac{\left(3 \pi t^{2}\right)}{2 \left(t\right)^{2}} \right)}\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=\sin\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=-1
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(t)&=\left(- 3 \left(t\right)\right)\cdot \left(6 \pi t\right) \\ &=- 18 \pi t^{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

The differential form uses the sum of these contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\int_{1}^{2}\left(A(t)+B(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{2}\left(- 18 \pi t^{2} - 1\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\left[- 6 \pi t^{3} - t\right]_{1}^{2} \\ &=\left(- 48 \pi - 2\right)-\left(- 6 \pi - 1\right) \\ &=- 42 \pi - 1
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
The path $C$ follows $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ from $A(0,0)$ to $B(1,1)$. Evaluate

$$
\int_C \left(- 4 y e^{x y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(-2\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Choose a coordinate parameter that keeps the curve smooth.

$$
x(t)=t^{3},\qquad y(t)=t.
$$

The stated endpoints give $t=0$ at $A$ and $t=1$ at $B$; retain that order in the integral. Differentiation gives

$$
x'(t)=3 t^{2},\qquad y'(t)=1.
$$

Write the coefficients of $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}y$ as $P$ and $Q$. Substitute both coordinates and multiply by the corresponding derivative. Denote the two contributions by $A(t)$ and $B(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(t)&=\left(- 4 \left(t\right) e^{\left(t^{3}\right) \left(t\right)}\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2}\right) \\ &=\left(- 4 t e^{t^{4}}\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2}\right) \\ &=- 12 t^{3} e^{t^{4}}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(t)&=\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=-2
\end{aligned}
$$

The differential form uses the sum of these contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\int_{0}^{1}\left(A(t)+B(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{1}\left(- 12 t^{3} e^{t^{4}} - 2\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\left[- 2 t - 3 e^{t^{4}}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=\left(- 3 e - 2\right)-\left(-3\right) \\ &=1 - 3 e
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
The path $C$ follows $y=x^{3} - 1$ from $A(2,7)$ to $B(1,0)$. Evaluate

$$
\int_C \left(- x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(y + 1\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Choose a coordinate parameter that keeps the curve smooth.

$$
x(t)=t,\qquad y(t)=t^{3} - 1.
$$

The stated endpoints give $t=2$ at $A$ and $t=1$ at $B$; retain that order in the integral. Differentiation gives

$$
x'(t)=1,\qquad y'(t)=3 t^{2}.
$$

Write the coefficients of $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}y$ as $P$ and $Q$. Substitute both coordinates and multiply by the corresponding derivative. Denote the two contributions by $A(t)$ and $B(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(t)&=\left(- \left(t\right)\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\ &=- t
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
B(t)&=\left(\left(t^{3} - 1\right) + 1\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2}\right) \\ &=3 t^{5}
\end{aligned}
$$

The differential form uses the sum of these contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\int_{2}^{1}\left(A(t)+B(t)\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{2}^{1}\left(3 t^{5} - t\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\left[\frac{t^{6}}{2} - \frac{t^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{1} \\ &=\left(0\right)-\left(30\right) \\ &=-30
\end{aligned}
$$
